title: A Nutritionist Investigates Persistent Bloating
script: Dr. Ratna: [professional] Bimo, you mentioned the bloating gets worse in the evenings. Has anything else changed recently besides your work schedule?
Bimo: [uncertain] Not that I've noticed, though I'll admit I haven't paid much attention to what I actually eat lately.
Dr. Ratna: [gently] That's fairly common. Most people can describe their symptoms in detail but struggle to recall what triggered them.
Bimo: [curious] So what would you recommend? I've read conflicting things online about cutting out entire food groups.
Dr. Ratna: [informative] Rather than eliminating everything at once, I'd suggest removing one likely trigger, dairy, for instance, for two weeks and observing carefully.
Bimo: [skeptical] Isn't that a bit slow? A friend of mine went gluten-free overnight and swore it transformed her digestion instantly.
Dr. Ratna: [patient] It might have, genuinely, but removing several things simultaneously makes it nearly impossible to identify which change actually mattered.
Bimo: [considering] That's fair. I suppose I was hoping for a quicker answer than methodically testing one variable at a time.
Dr. Ratna: [warmly] Understandable, though the gut tends to reward patience far more reliably than it rewards drastic overnight changes.
Bimo: [honest] Two weeks without cheese sounds miserable, if I'm being completely honest with you.
Dr. Ratna: [amused] Most people say exactly that, and most people survive it perfectly well, occasionally even feeling noticeably better by the end.
Bimo: [thoughtful] And if dairy turns out not to be the problem, what happens then?
Dr. Ratna: [explaining] Then we reintroduce it and move to the next likely culprit, gluten or excess sugar, following the same method.
Bimo: [worried] Could this actually be something more serious, something I should be more concerned about?
Dr. Ratna: [reassuring] It's unlikely, given your other results, but if the elimination approach doesn't clarify things, we'll investigate further with proper testing.
Bimo: [relieved] That's reassuring, actually. I think I expected you to say something far more alarming.
Dr. Ratna: [encouraging] Keep a simple food diary alongside this, noting symptoms honestly, even the embarrassing ones you might want to leave out.
Bimo: [laughing] Noted, though I make no promises about how honest that diary will be on weekends.
Dr. Ratna: [smiling] I'll take partial honesty over none at all. Let's review everything together in two weeks.

quiz.question: What method does Dr. Ratna recommend instead of cutting out everything at once?
options: Eliminating all food groups immediately
Removing one likely trigger at a time and observing carefully
Ignoring the symptoms entirely
Only taking medication
quiz.explanation: She recommends removing one likely trigger, like dairy, for two weeks and observing carefully rather than eliminating everything at once.

quiz.question: Why does Dr. Ratna caution against removing several foods simultaneously?
options: It's too expensive
It makes it nearly impossible to identify which change actually mattered
It's against medical guidelines
It takes too much time to prepare meals
quiz.explanation: She explains that removing several things at once makes it nearly impossible to identify which change actually mattered.

quiz.question: What does Dr. Ratna say about the gut and patience?
options: The gut prefers sudden, drastic changes
The gut tends to reward patience more than drastic overnight changes
Patience has no effect on digestion
Only medication works
quiz.explanation: She says the gut tends to reward patience far more reliably than it rewards drastic overnight changes.

quiz.question: What happens if dairy turns out not to be the problem?
options: The process ends immediately
They reintroduce it and test the next likely culprit, like gluten
Bimo must see a different doctor
They repeat the same test with dairy
quiz.explanation: Dr. Ratna explains they would reintroduce dairy and move to the next likely culprit using the same method.

quiz.question: What does Dr. Ratna ask Bimo to keep alongside the elimination process?
options: An exercise log
A simple food diary noting symptoms honestly
A sleep tracker
A list of medications
quiz.explanation: She asks him to keep a simple food diary alongside the elimination process, noting symptoms honestly.
